name: Table read by antidiagonals. T(n,k) is the least number coprime to all numbers in [n+1, n+k].
reference: Paul Erdős, Some of my favourite unsolved problems. Math. Japon. (1997), 527-537.
Paul Erdős and Ronald Graham, Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathématique (1980).
link: S. A. Burr, P. Erdős, R. L. Graham, and W. Wen-Ching Li, Complete sequences of sets of integer powers, Acta Arith. (1996), 133-138.
formula: For all m < k, T(m*k,k) - T(m*k,k-1) > 0 iff k is prime.
Conjecture of Erdős and Pomerance: T(n,k) < (1+o(1)) * log(n), for fixed k >= 2 and sufficiently large n.
Conjecture of Erdős and Pomerance: there exists epsilon>0, such that T(n,log(n)) >= (2+epsilon)*log(n) infinitely often.
author: _Elijah Beregovsky_, Dec 16 2025
